intro: Two teams of eleven use hooked sticks to drive a hard ball into the opponents' goal. Only the flat face of the stick may touch the ball, goals can only be scored from inside the shooting circle, and set-piece penalty corners are a major source of goals. The International Hockey Federation (FIH) publishes the Rules of Hockey.
inThirtySeconds: Score only with a shot touched by an attacker inside the shooting circle.
Play the ball with the flat side of the stick — never with the rounded back or your feet.
No offside: attackers can wait anywhere.
Defensive fouls in or near the circle give penalty corners.
objective: Score more goals than the opponent in four 15-minute quarters.

facts.players: 11 per team (10 + goalkeeper), unlimited rolling substitutions

scoring.label: Field goal
scoring.detail: Ball played by an attacker inside the circle and crossing the goal line.

scoring.label: Penalty corner goal
scoring.detail: Goal from the set piece after a defensive foul.

scoring.label: Penalty stroke
scoring.detail: A one-on-one shot against the goalkeeper from the penalty spot.

bodies.name: International Hockey Federation
bodies.scope: World governing body; publishes the Rules of Hockey

chapters.title: Playing the ball
chapters.summary: The stick, the feet and the circle.

rules.title: Flat side only
rules.summary: Players may only play the ball with the flat face and edges of the stick, not the rounded back.
rules.body: This is why players turn their stick over to play on the 'reverse' side. Using the back of the stick gives the opponents a free hit.

rules.title: No feet
rules.summary: Field players must not stop, kick or propel the ball with any part of the body.
rules.body: It is only an offence if the player gains an advantage or moved deliberately into the ball's path. Goalkeepers may use their body inside their own circle.

rules.title: Scoring from the circle
rules.summary: A goal only counts if the ball was played by an attacker inside the shooting circle and wasn't played outside the circle afterwards.
rules.body: The circle is a D-shaped area extending 14.63 m (16 yards) from the goal. A spectacular shot from outside does not count unless deflected by an attacker inside the circle.
rules.example: A powerful hit from just outside the circle flies into the net untouched: no goal, it's a restart for the defence.

chapters.title: Set pieces
chapters.summary: Free hits, penalty corners and penalty strokes.

rules.title: Free hits and self-pass
rules.summary: Fouls give a free hit; opponents must be 5 m away, and the taker may dribble it themselves (self-pass).
rules.body: Free hits to attackers inside the 23 m area have special rules: the ball must travel 5 m or be touched by a defender before entering the circle.

rules.title: Penalty corner
rules.summary: Awarded for defensive fouls inside the circle (that don't prevent a likely goal) or deliberate fouls in the defending 23 m area.
rules.body: An attacker pushes the ball from the back line, 10 m from the goal post. Five defenders, including the goalkeeper, start behind the goal line; the rest wait beyond the halfway line. Attackers must stop the ball outside the circle before shooting, and the first shot, if a hit, must not cross the goal line above backboard height.

rules.title: Penalty stroke
rules.summary: Awarded when a foul prevents a probable goal, or for deliberate fouls in the circle against a player with the ball.
rules.body: Taken from the spot 6.4 m in front of the goal: one attacker against the goalkeeper on the line, with one push or flick.

rules.title: Green, yellow and red cards
rules.summary: Green card: 2-minute suspension. Yellow card: at least 5 minutes. Red card: permanent.
rules.body: Dangerous play with raised balls or swinging sticks, and misconduct, are the most common reasons. Suspended players' teams play short.

fouls.name: Back stick
fouls.description: Playing the ball with the rounded back of the stick.

fouls.name: Foot foul
fouls.description: Ball deliberately or advantageously played with the body.
fouls.consequence: Free hit (penalty corner in the circle)

fouls.name: Obstruction
fouls.description: Shielding the ball with the body or stick to block a tackle.

fouls.name: Dangerous play
fouls.description: Raised ball or stick endangering others.

flow.title: Centre pass
flow.description: Each quarter and each goal restarts with a pass from the centre.

flow.title: Quarters
flow.description: Four 15-minute quarters with short breaks and a half-time interval.

flow.title: Penalty corners
flow.description: Rehearsed set pieces with drag flicks and deflections.

flow.title: Shoot-out
flow.description: Knockout matches level after time go to a one-on-one shoot-out.

positions.name: Goalkeeper
positions.role: Fully padded; may use the body to save inside the circle.

positions.name: Defenders
positions.role: Protect the circle and run penalty-corner defence.

positions.name: Midfielders
positions.role: Link play and cover huge distances.

positions.name: Forwards
positions.role: Score from inside the circle and win penalty corners.

field.name: Pitch
notes: Shooting circles 14.63 m from the goal

glossary.definition: A powerful scooping shot used at penalty corners.
Playing with the stick turned over, on the left side.
Taking a free hit by dribbling the ball yourself.

funFacts: Field hockey's quarters replaced two halves in international play in 2014.
India and Pakistan dominated Olympic men's hockey for decades; India won eight golds.
